newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Finmin Zalm hits out at German gold plan.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Finmin Zalm hits out at German gold plan.

text.p: Dutch finance minister Gerrit Zalm said on Thursday a German plan to reduce the country's government deficit by revaluing central bank gold reserves would endanger the soundness of a future European single currency.
"It is all about preparing for the start of EMU in a sound and orderly manner and meeting the Maastricht criteria in a proper manner," he told Dutch television news.
"If that is accomplished by accounting tricks then the soundness of the whole EMU process is in danger."

The controversial plan announced last week involves revaluing Bundesbank gold closer to market rates, generating a book windfall to plug holes in Germany's finances and improve its chances of qualifying for monetary union.

"It makes me worried that these kind of measures are being considered," Zalm told the NRC Handelsblad newspaper in an interview. "I can't imagine that Germany wants to qualify for EMU, with regard to the budget deficit, in this way."
"I trust that Germany will reach the goal of a maximum three percent deficit in 1997, not through a one-off windfall from the Bundesbank, but rather by spending limits and increased tax revenues."
The paper said Zalm, currently chairman of the European Council of Finance Ministers, planned to travel to Bonn soon to seek further details from German Finance Minister Theo Waigel.
